title: POC weekly sync - model selection & pinning
header:
Date: 2026-08-11
Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Avery Kim (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood CSM); Maya Patel (NovaFin Head of ML), Tom Briggs (Platform), Lisa Chen (Security), Evan Park (PM)
summary: Weekly POC sync to review model perf comparisons across catalog variants, confirm pinning strategy for pilot traffic, and plan rollback/fallback tests. Discussed latency vs cost tradeoffs, quantization impacts, and security checklist items. Agreed to pin v2.1 for canary and run rollback exercise on staging next week.
action_items: Maya Patel | Share internal eval set + failure cases | 2026-08-13
Diego Ramos | Run rollback test on staging and document steps | 2026-08-18
Avery Kim | Send pricing delta for v2.1 pinned vs dynamic routing | 2026-08-12
next_steps: Redwood to pin model catalog: start canary on v2.1 for 10% traffic next sprint
Customer to validate canary outputs and share counterexamples
Run rollback/fallback drill on staging with SE (Diego)
Send security docs and SOC2 evidence to Lisa
transcript:
[00:00] Avery Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:07] Maya Patel: Hey, Maya here.
[00:09] Tom Briggs: Tom from platform.
[00:11] Lisa Chen: Lisa, security.
[00:13] Evan Park: Evan, PM.
[00:15] Diego Ramos: Diego from Redwood SE.
[00:18] Avery Kim: Cool. Agenda — model perf recap, pinning plan, rollbacks/fallbacks, security questions, next steps.
[00:30] Priya Nair: Also wanted to flag timeline check — pilot closes end of month.
[01:02] Avery Kim: Great. Diego, can you walk through the catalog comparison we ran last week?
[01:12] Diego Ramos: Sure. We compared four variants from the Redwood catalog: base-1.0 (float32), base-1.0-quant (int4-ish quant), v2.0 (updated weights) and v2.1 (latest fine-tuned with instruction tuning). The key metrics were latency p50/p95, token cost, and a quality score derived from your eval set — which Maya shared partially.
[01:35] Maya Patel: Minor note — the eval set has been expanded, happy to drop the full set after call.
[01:40] Diego Ramos: Perfect. Results summary: v2.1 has best quality (lower hallucination rate on your counterexamples) but 10-15% higher p95 latency compared to base-1.0-quant. Quantized base had lowest cost but we saw some failure modes on longer-context prompts, likely KV cache mishandling in that quant path. There were some transcription oddities in the logs — redwood console labeled a few traces as 'k-v cache' vs 'kvchache' in places, apologies for noise.
[02:12] Tom Briggs: When you say failure modes, is that correctness drop or timeouts?
[02:18] Diego Ramos: Mostly correctness — hallucinations and occasional token repetition with >2k context. Not many timeouts.
[02:24] Maya Patel: That's concerning — our production prompts are long, average 1.8k tokens.
[02:30] Diego Ramos: Right, so recommendations: pin canary to v2.1 for high-quality, but for tail-latency sensitive routes we can route to base-1.0-quant or base-1.0 depending on tolerance. Also we can enable prefix KV caching to reduce repeated context cost.
[02:50] Lisa Chen: From security perspective, we need to confirm data residency and logs — which of these variants run in Dedicated vs Hosted?
[02:58] Avery Kim: Good call. For this pilot you're on Redwood Dedicated in our us-west pool, everything stays in your VPC peering. We will provide audit logs and the KMS integration notes.
[03:12] Lisa Chen: Please send the SOC2 artifacts again. We couldn't find the latest cert in the portal.
[03:17] Avery Kim: Will do, I'll resend the security bundle — Priya, can you pick this up?
[03:21] Priya Nair: Yep — uploading to the shared folder after the call.
[03:25] Evan Park: Quick question on rollback — how fast can we switch traffic back if v2.1 misbehaves?
[03:30] Diego Ramos: We support instant routing changes via the console API; in practice we've seen sub-10s switching for route rules. But we always recommend a staged rollback: pin to a safe variant, then verify traces for 5-10 minutes before full cutover.
[03:45] Tom Briggs: Can you document the rollback steps? We want runbook for on-call.
[03:48] Diego Ramos: Absolutely — I'll run a rollback drill on staging and create a runbook.
[04:00] Maya Patel: What about model pinning semantics? If we pin to v2.1, does Redwood still auto-patch minor infra changes or is it fully pinned?
[04:10] Avery Kim: Pinning locks model version for inference. Infra patches like runtime security patches will still apply. We won't auto-upgrade model weights without explicit rollout.
[04:20] Maya Patel: Good. We also want a fallback policy where if latency crosses threshold, route to cheaper variant automatically. Is that supported?
[04:28] Diego Ramos: Yes, Smart routing rules can do latency-based routing. You can set SLOs and fallback targets. Note: automatically routing to a quantized model can change output distribution; recommend a canary and compare outputs via your eval harness.
[04:45] Evan Park: About measurement — how did you compute the 'quality score'?
[04:50] Diego Ramos: It's a weighted metric combining BLEU-like ngram overlap for structured prompts, plus a hallucination penalty derived from your labeled failures. It's in the spreadsheet we shared.
[04:58] Maya Patel: There were a few examples where the quant model hallucinated bank names — that's a dealbreaker.
[05:05] Avery Kim: Understood. That argues for pinning v2.1 for those sensitive routes. We can do per-route pinning.
[05:12] Tom Briggs: Cost question — how big is the price delta contending with v2.1 vs base-1.0-quant for our traffic estimate?
[05:18] Avery Kim: Preliminary numbers: roughly +22% token cost for v2.1 vs quantized base on your workload. Diego will send more granular per-token and per-hour projections.
[05:28] Diego Ramos: I'll attach the cost sheet and broken down by route in the drive.
[05:31] Lisa Chen: Also need data retention policy for traces and full request payloads. We want minimal storage for PII.
[05:36] Diego Ramos: By default logs are 30 days, but for Dedicated we can configure retention and mask request bodies. We'll include masking options in the docs.
[05:45] Maya Patel: For the canary — we're good to run 10% traffic on v2.1 for two days and then expand if perf looks good.
[05:52] Avery Kim: Sounds good. Diego, can you set up the canary and pin config in the dev environment?
[05:57] Diego Ramos: I'll set up a canary rule: 10% traffic to v2.1, 90% to current baseline, with latency SLO of p95 < 700ms; fallback on breach to base-1.0. I'll also enable detailed tracing for first 1k requests.
[06:12] Tom Briggs: Please include trace sampling and link to the tracing console.
[06:15] Diego Ramos: Will do.
[06:18] Priya Nair: Lisa, I uploaded the SOC artifacts and the access control doc; check your email.
[06:24] Lisa Chen: Got it, will review.
[06:26] Maya Patel: One last thing — can we test rollback scenario where v2.1 gets a spike in hallucination? I'd like to see cold-starts and the rollback happen.
[06:35] Diego Ramos: We'll simulate via the staging harness — inject failure cases and flip the rule. Expect to document time to full rollback and any logs created.
[06:44] Avery Kim: Excellent. To recap: pin v2.1 for canary at 10%, run rollback drill on staging next Tues (Diego/Tom), Maya to share full eval set by Friday, Avery to send pricing sheet and SOC2 artifacts, and Diego to create runbook.
[06:59] Evan Park: I'm adding those items to our tracker. Thanks.
[07:03] Maya Patel: Thanks all.
[07:05] Avery Kim: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up by email with the links and timelines.
[07:10] [meeting ends]
questions: How quickly can we rollback if v2.1 misbehaves?
Can we auto-fallback by latency SLO to a quantized model?
What is the exact cost delta for pinning v2.1?
